name: ai.axad/language-tutor
title: Axad
description: AI language tutor: lessons, flash cards with spaced review, voice, Dutch inburgering practice.

tools.name: browse_catalog
tools.description: Browse Axad's library of lessons and practice exams. With no lang, returns the languages Axad teaches. With lang, returns the sections and lessons at path in that language's tree (an empty path is its top). For a learner who wants something to study or works toward an exam. Axad's API docs: https://axad.ai/developers.

lang.description: BCP 47 code of the language to learn: "nl".

path.description: Section names from the top of the language's tree: ["Inburgering", "A2"].

tools.name: open_lesson
tools.description: Open a lesson and read where the learner is in it: a lesson of Axad's library (lesson), one the learner already has (material), or a new lesson made from a text they supply (text). Returns the current page's text or the first 40 sentences, and starter suggestions. It counts as one of the plan's active lessons until closed.

lang.description: With text: BCP 47 code of the text's language.

lesson.description: A lesson id from Axad's library.

material.description: A material id of a lesson the learner already has.

text.description: The learner's own text to study: an article, a letter, a message.

title.description: With text: a short title in the text's language.

tools.name: list_lessons
tools.description: List the learner's lessons, the active ones first, then the closed ones, each with its language, page and progress. For a learner who wants to go on with something they studied.

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Read one page of a lesson that has pages (a practice exam: one question and its text a page) and keep the learner's place there; for a lesson with no pages, read sentences from..to (at most 40). Returns the page text, or the numbered sentences.

from.description: No pages: the first sentence number.

page.description: 0-based page; omit for the learner's current page.

to.description: No pages: the last sentence number.

tools.name: close_lesson
tools.description: Close a lesson the learner finished or set aside. Its place, chats and cards are kept, and it no longer counts against the plan's active lessons; opening it again by its material id reopens it. Returns the lesson's state and the active count.

tools.name: save_cards
tools.description: Save flash cards to the learner's bag: words, phrases, idioms, sentences or patterns they engaged with, at or just above their level. Takes 1 to 6 cards a call, each with its front, back and the sentence where it was met; a card already in the bag gets the new example. Returns the saved and skipped cards and the bag's count and limit.

back.description: The meaning, at most 6 words, in the learner's support language.

example.description: The sentence where the learner met it, copied exactly.

front.description: The card's general form: a word's dictionary form (a noun with de/het where the language needs it), a pattern's frame with … for the open part.

image.description: A library picture id, or the concept a picture was requested under.

key.description: The dictionary form, lowercase; a pattern's frame ("om … te").

kind.description: One of: word (one word, in its dictionary form), phrase (a fixed group of words whose meaning comes from its words: a collocation or set expression, "een afspraak maken"), idiom (a fixed expression whose meaning does not come from its words, "iets onder de knie hebben"), sentence (a whole sentence or clause with its verb, kept as met), pattern (a structure with open slots, "om … te"), rule (how a part of the grammar works), exception (a form that breaks a rule), concept (a named idea of the language or its culture: a split verb, de/het), tip (a way to learn or to pass the exam). Choose the most specific one that fits. A whole sentence or clause with its verb is a sentence, never a phrase; a phrase or idiom is a unit smaller than that. A fixed group whose meaning you get by reading its words is a phrase; one whose meaning you cannot get from its words is an idiom. Another word only if none fits.

lang.description: BCP 47 code of the card's language.

material.description: The lesson the cards come from, when there is one.

tools.name: due_cards
tools.description: List the learner's flash cards that are due for review now, the most overdue first, each with an example sentence. lang limits it to one language and limit (1 to 20, default 10) caps the number. Returns the cards and the total due.

tools.name: review_card
tools.description: Record how well the learner recalled a card: 1 forgot, 2 hard, 3 good, 4 easy. Schedules the card's next review (FSRS) and returns its due date.

tools.name: speak
tools.description: Make a natural voice recording of a sentence in the language the learner learns. Returns a link to the audio and the start and end time of each word. It spends a little credit; each recording is kept, so the same sentence again is free.

voice.description: A speaker label of the language ("Vrouw", "Man"); omit for the narrator.

tools.name: list_runbooks
tools.description: List Axad's learning paths (daily review, exam path, page by page, free-form chat), with the learner's place in each when signed in.

tools.name: start_runbook
tools.description: Start a learning path for the learner in a language, or return their place in it if they started it before. Returns the current step: what it asks, which tools and widgets it uses, and when it is done.

tools.name: next_step
tools.description: Read the learner's current step in a learning path they started, without moving it. Returns the step: what it asks, which tools and widgets it uses, and when it is done.

tools.name: record_step
tools.description: Record how the current step of a learning path went (done, skipped or struggled) with an optional note, and move the learner on. Returns the next step, or that the path is finished.

note.description: What the learner found hard, in a few words.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Return the learner's Axad account: their plan, its limits and what they use of them (cards in the bag, active lessons), and their credit spent and allowance.

tools.name: upgrade_link
tools.description: Return a link on axad.ai where the learner can pick a plan, add a card for more free use, or buy credit; want says which. Returns the url and a short text.

tools.name: redeem_gift
tools.description: Redeem a gift code the learner was given: what it gives is added to their account at once (credit, more cards in the bag, more open practices; any of them may be 0), and the code is used up for good. Returns what the code added and the new credit.

tools.name: axad_developer_feedback
tools.description: Sends a short report to Axad's developers about Axad itself: a bug, an issue, a shortcoming, a missing feature, a gap or an idea, found by the agent or wished for by the learner. Returns the report's id. For an agent that met a fault in an Axad tool or a wish Axad does not cover.

expected.description: What should have happened instead, in your own words. Leave out names, emails and other personal details.

happened.description: What happened, or what the learner wants, in your own words. Leave out names, emails, phone numbers and other personal details.

kind.description: What sort of report it is.

source.description: Who found it or wished for it: the agent (a fault it met, an idea of its own) or the learner (something they asked for).

summary.description: The report in one line, in your own words. Leave out names, emails and other personal details.

tool.description: The Axad tool or widget it is about, if any.

tools.name: search_bag
tools.description: Search the learner's flash cards by words in the card's language or by a short meaning. Returns the matching cards, up to limit (default 10, at most 30); lang restricts the search to one language.

lang.description: BCP 47 code: only cards in this language.

query.description: Words in the card's language, or a short meaning: "nunca", "double negatives".

tools.name: find_images
tools.description: Search the shared image library for pictures that show a word, chunk, action or scene. query is a literal English description of the picture and lang the language of the concept. Returns up to 8 pictures, best fit first, each with a library id, title and concept.

concept.description: The language element it should teach, in its language: "la sala de espera".

lang.description: BCP 47 code of the concept: pictures with words in another language are left out.

query.description: A literal English description of the picture you want: "a patient in a doctor's waiting room, reading a magazine".

tools.name: nominate_image
tools.description: Ask for a picture of a generic concept every learner shares: a concrete thing, action, place or everyday scene. Returns an existing library picture when one stands for the concept; otherwise checks the request against the library's rules and draws a new one, which fills in when ready (this spends credit). canon names the concept in 1 to 4 English words.

canon.description: The generic English concept the picture shows, 1–4 words, dictionary form, with no names, numbers or words of one sentence: "doctor's practice", "apple", "train platform". The library keeps one picture per canon.

concept.description: The language element it teaches, 1–8 words in its language: "cancelar", "la sala de espera". The `image` fields that show this picture hold these words.

prompt.description: What to draw, 40–200 English words: the scene, each object and where it is, what the people do. Concrete, drawable and generic: no names, clock times, dates or numbers (except quoted `text`); no style words.

text.description: Only when words in the picture are the lesson: at most 6 words in `lang`, also written in the prompt in double quotes. Omit it for a picture with no words, which serves every language.

title.description: One literal English sentence of 8–40 words: who, what, where. Generic, with no names, numbers, clock times or dates. Search reads it.

tools.name: show_cards
tools.description: Shows Axad's answer as one stack of cards, as the Axad app does: use it for every reply that teaches a language the learner learns, instead of answering in plain text. Use it at once when the learner's message is only text in that language, such as a pasted Dutch sentence with no request: that is a Dig in: gloss-chunks of the whole text open, with its translation; explain open, for the one thing worth learning; quiz, tips and examples with fold true; next: its forms, a contrast ("«X» or «Y»?"), other ways to say it, and Dig into the next sentence. Any other reply: the 1 or 2 cards that answer best open, 2 or 3 more that help with fold true (one title row until a tap opens it), and up to 5 next buttons for what else would help (label is the button's text, ask the message a tap sends). One call per reply, with lang ("nl") and cards: 1 to 6 items, each a widget with its props, in the order to show them. A message "Dig in: «…»", "Examples: «…»", "Other ways: «…»", "Quiz me: «…»", "Breakdown: «…»" or "Explain more: «…»" comes from a tap in a widget: it acts on the quoted words only, and hidden context {selection, sentence} says where they were.

cards.description: The stack, in the order to show it: each card is one widget with its props.

anyOf.description: Displays how a span of the target language is built, for a learner who wants to see it: the text split into chunks, a literal gloss for each word, links between parts that stand apart, and a translation of the span.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays 3 to 6 example sentences of a word, chunk or pattern at work, for a learner who wants to see it in use. Each has its translation and the target part marked, and may have a picture.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays other ways to say the same thing, for a learner who wants to sound more natural or find a simpler form: the original and 2 to 5 alternatives, each tagged by kind, such as simpler or more formal.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays a short explanation of one rule, exception or tip that explains what the learner met: a title, a few points and an optional small table.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays tips that help a learner keep or use what they met: a tip for their exam, how people use it, or a memory trick, with an optional example sentence.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays two or three look-alike forms side by side, for a learner confused by the difference: one row per side with examples, and a test to tell them apart.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays a reusable sentence frame with slots, the fillers that fit each slot, and sentences built from it, for a learner who met a pattern they can use with other words.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays the forms of one word as a table, for a learner who asks about them: verb conjugation, article or gender, plural, comparative or diminutive.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays a check of the learner's own writing in a language they learn: what they wrote, the corrected text with the changes marked, a short reason for each fix, and a more natural version.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays one quick question for the learner to use what was just shown: choice, cloze, order or translate. The view checks the answer and shows the result with an explanation.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Plays short lines of the target language one by one and pauses after each for the learner to say it aloud, with each line's meaning.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Plays a line or short dialogue for the learner to listen to, with the transcript hidden until shown or answered. It can limit replays like an exam's listening part, ask one question, or serve as repeat-after-me practice.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays one library picture of a concrete word, chunk, action or scene, with the words it teaches, for a learner who remembers better with an image.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays a role-play of a real situation, such as calling the doctor or asking the way, for a learner who wants to practise a conversation: 4 to 8 lines where the learner plays B and sees each B line on request.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays one sentence split into the places its words take, for a learner who asks about word order: slots such as subject and verbs, the verb places marked, and a note on the rule.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays the grammar structure of one sentence, for a learner who wants to see how it is built: each part with its role and word class, and the kind of each clause.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays one message in a formal and an informal version, for a learner who asks how to say it politely or casually: the changed words are marked, with a note on who gets which.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays one practice item in an exam's own format, for a learner who wants exam practice: a short text, a question, options and an optional timer. The view checks the pick and shows the explanation.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays one library picture of a place or situation with its 3 to 6 key words beside it, for a learner who wants the vocabulary of a waiting room, a pharmacy or a kitchen.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays a chart for a learner who needs to see how things relate: a verb grid across tenses, a time line, a sentence tree or a topic map.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays a small layout built from blocks (say, text, table, list, image), for a learner who asks for something the other widgets do not show, such as a grid of prices or a mini dictionary of one theme.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

anyOf.description: Displays 1 to 6 one-click next steps under a reply: further asks the learner might make, and the next text to study. Clicking an item sends its message.

fold.description: true: a secondary card, shown as its title row until one tap opens it. Omit on the main cards.

lang.description: BCP 47 code of the language the cards teach: "nl". The view speaks and saves their words in it.

next.description: Up to 5 one-tap next steps shown under the stack: label is the button's text, ask the message a tap sends.

ask.description: The message a tap sends, in the learner's words.

tools.name: show_home
tools.description: Displays Axad's start menu as a list of taps: go on with the open lesson, start a lesson, paste a sentence, inburgering practice, review cards, the bag. Signed in, it says how many cards are due and which lesson is open. It is the start for a greeting or a first turn with nothing to study; a message that holds a sentence to study is not one.

lang.description: BCP 47 code of the language to learn: "nl" (the default).

next.description: Up to 3 one-tap next steps shown under the widget: label is the button's text, ask the message a tap sends.

ask.description: The message a tap sends, in the learner's words.

tools.name: show_review
tools.description: Displays the learner's due flash cards one at a time: the front, the answer and example on a tap, then four taps to grade the recall, which schedules the card's next review. Needs the learner's account.

lang.description: BCP 47 code of the cards' language: "nl" (the default).

limit.description: How many cards to load, at most 20.

next.description: Up to 3 one-tap next steps shown under the widget: label is the button's text, ask the message a tap sends.

ask.description: The message a tap sends, in the learner's words.

tools.name: show_drill
tools.description: Displays a short practice round for the learner to answer by tapping, one question at a time: choice, cloze, order or translate. It shows the progress and a score at the end. Takes 2 to 10 questions, each shaped as a quiz widget's props, and shows them as given.

items.description: The questions, in the order to ask them.

lang.description: BCP 47 code of the language the questions teach: "nl".

next.description: Up to 3 one-tap next steps shown under the widget: label is the button's text, ask the message a tap sends.

ask.description: The message a tap sends, in the learner's words.

title.description: What the round practises, in a few words.
